content.overview: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is an umbrella statute empowering the Central Government to protect and improve environmental quality and to prevent, control and abate pollution. Section 3 is the principal enabling power. Section 7 prohibits persons carrying on any industry, operation or process from discharging or emitting environmental pollutants in excess of prescribed standards. Section 8 regulates handling of hazardous substances. Section 15 provides penalties for contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions.
content.glance: Ask: (1) s. 3 Central measure? (2) s. 7 emission/discharge beyond standards? (3) s. 8 hazardous handling? (4) s. 15 penalty?
content.study:
EPA is the general environmental statute; Water Act and Air Act remain medium-specific. NGT Schedule I includes the EPA for civil environmental questions.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: s. 3 powers
sections.body: Central Government may take all measures necessary or expedient to protect and improve the environment and to prevent, control and abate pollution.

sections.heading: s. 7 standards
sections.body: No person carrying on industry, operation or process shall discharge or emit environmental pollutants in excess of prescribed standards.

sections.heading: s. 8 hazardous substances
sections.body: Persons handling hazardous substances must comply with prescribed procedures and safeguards.

sections.heading: s. 15 penalty
sections.body: Contravention of the Act, rules, orders or directions attracts penalty as enacted (imprisonment, fine, or both — verify current text).

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: EPA coexists with Water Act, Air Act and NGT; identify the medium and the correct statute on the facts.

examples.title: Excess emission
examples.body: Factory emits pollutants above prescribed standards — s. 7 breach; penalty under s. 15; Central directions may flow from s. 3 framework.

hypotheticals.question: Does the EPA replace the need for Water Act consent for a discharge into a stream?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not automatically. Water Act and EPA can apply concurrently; match the medium and the specific statutory duty on the facts.

distinctions.title: EPA umbrella vs Water/Air sector statutes
distinctions.left: General environmental protection and standards under EPA.
distinctions.right: Medium-specific consent and board regulation under Water Act / Air Act.

misconceptions.trap: EPA is only about criminal penalty under s. 15.
misconceptions.correction: s. 3 enabling powers and ss. 7–8 substantive duties are central; s. 15 is the penalty provision.
